# Ryvax.js — AI-native framework context

> This file is the compact source of truth for coding agents. Ryvax.js is a React-first full-stack TypeScript framework with file-based routing, Node HTTP execution, SSR, static generation, streaming, typed API handlers, Server Actions, SQL/auth/security contracts, and portable deployment output.

## Non-negotiable identity

- Package: `@kvantjs/ryvax.js`
- Repository: `https://github.com/kvantjs/ryvax.js`
- Runtime baseline: Node.js 20 or newer.
- Language: TypeScript. Project modules use ESM (`"type": "module"`).
- UI runtime: React and React DOM.
- Core dependencies: `chokidar`, `esbuild`, `react`, `react-dom`, and `zod`.
- License: MIT.
- Current public package exports are `.`, `./client`, `./web`, `./seo`, and `./adapters`.
- The framework owns route discovery, compilation, request context, HTTP dispatch, rendering, manifests, and runtime lifecycle. The application owns domain rules, validation policy, provider credentials, and business persistence.

## Agent priority order

1. Inspect the existing project before editing.
2. Follow this repository's implementation and `package.json` exports.
3. Follow the exact documentation pages and tests.
4. Prefer the smallest native Ryvax change.
5. Treat uncertainty as uncertainty; do not invent an API, directory, command, provider, or guarantee.
6. Run typecheck, tests, and build when the project provides them.

## Canonical project structure

| Path | Meaning | Agent rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pages/` | Legacy/file-based page and API routes. | Use for the documented pages-router style. |
| `app/` | App Router-compatible pages and API route files. | Route files are `page.*` and `route.*`; layouts and boundaries live here. |
| `actions/` | Server Actions. | A source file is discovered only when it contains `'use server'`. |
| `src/` | Application components, client entry, and reusable code. | Do not assume every `src` file is a route. |
| `public/` | Public static assets. | Refer to assets by their public URL. |
| `framework.config.ts` | Optional app configuration. | Supported extensions are `.ts`, `.mts`, `.js`, and `.mjs`. |
| `.meu/` | Default development/build manifest and bundles. | Generated; never edit manually. |
| `dist/` | Static export or deployment package. | Generated; never edit manually. |
| `migrations/` | SQL migration files created by `ryvax migrate create`. | Preserve paired `.up.sql` and `.down.sql` files. |

The compiler ignores source files beginning with `_` during route discovery. App route groups `(group)` and parallel-slot directories beginning with `@` do not become URL segments. Do not create `next.config.*`, `vite.config.*`, or a React Router tree unless the application explicitly adds and owns such tooling.

## Routing contract

Ryvax discovers source files under `pages/` and `app/`. In `pages/`, the file path maps directly to the URL; `index`, `page`, and `route` are terminal aliases and are removed from the pathname. In `app/`, only files named `page.*` or `route.*` are routes; `layout`, `error`, `forbidden`, `unauthorized`, `loading`, and `not-found` are boundaries or layouts.

Examples:

```text
pages/index.tsx                 -> /
pages/about.tsx                 -> /about
pages/api/health.ts             -> /api/health
pages/users/[id].tsx            -> /users/:id
pages/docs/[...parts].tsx       -> /docs/*parts
pages/docs/[[...parts]].tsx    -> /docs/*parts? (optional)
app/dashboard/page.tsx          -> /dashboard
app/dashboard/route.ts          -> /dashboard (HTTP API route)
app/dashboard/[id]/page.tsx     -> /dashboard/:id
```

Dynamic parameters are decoded strings in `context.params`. Catch-all parameters are decoded string arrays. Query parameters are `context.query` (`URLSearchParams`), and the complete URL is `context.url`. Static routes outrank dynamic routes; dynamic routes outrank catch-all routes; API routes are sorted before page routes. Always verify the result with `npx ryvax routes --json`.

## Rendering contract

A page module exports a default component `(props, context) => ReactNode | Promise<ReactNode>`. It may export `getServerSideProps(context)`, `getStaticProps()`, `getStaticPaths()`, `generateStaticParams()`, `revalidate`, and `headers`. `getServerSideProps` is preferred when request data is needed. `getStaticProps` is used for static data. Dynamic static generation requires `getStaticPaths` or `generateStaticParams`.

The `RequestContext` contains `request`, `response`, `signal`, `url`, `params`, `query`, `headers`, `body`, `runtime`, `state`, `env`, and optional `requestId`, `deadline`, and `timeoutMs`. Propagate `context.signal` into cancellable work. `revalidate` enables response caching; do not cache private or authorization-dependent output without an explicit policy.

The client entry is discovered from `src/client.ts`, `src/client.tsx`, `src/client.js`, or `src/client.jsx` and is bundled to `/_meu/static/client.js`. Use the `./client` package export for hydration, navigation, and HMR helpers. A module beginning with `'use client'` is checked by the RSC boundary validator; do not import server-only modules into it.

## API contract

Use `pages/api/*.ts` for a pages-style API or `app/**/route.ts` for an App Router API. Export one or more method handlers typed as `ApiHandler`:

```ts
import type { ApiHandler } from '@kvantjs/ryvax.js';

export const GET: ApiHandler = async ({ query, env, signal }) => ({
  status: 200,
  headers: { 'Cache-Control': 'no-store' },
  json: { ok: true, q: query.get('q'), environment: env.NODE_ENV ?? 'development', aborted: signal.aborted }
});
```

Supported named methods are `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`, and `HEAD`; a `default` handler is also supported. Return `ResponseLike` fields: `status`, `statusText`, `headers`, `body`, `json`, `react`, `redirect`, `stream`, `signal`, and `tags`. `context.body` is parsed by the runtime for request bodies. Validate it before domain work. Unsupported methods produce 405 with `Allow`; missing routes produce 404. API 404 responses use JSON `{ "error": "Route not found" }`.

API middleware is exported as `middleware` from the API module. Global middleware is configured with `framework.config.*`. Do not create Express middleware or a separate server to replace the Ryvax request pipeline.

## Configuration and commands

`loadConfig` reads `.env` and `.env.local`, then compiles the first existing `framework.config.ts`, `.mts`, `.js`, or `.mjs`. Config values are typed through `AppConfig`; environment values are strings and must be parsed/validated by the application. Relevant options include `port`, `host`, `runtime`, security headers, `cache`, `middleware`, `env`, logging, observability, health/readiness, limits, actions, deployment target, and plugins.

```bash
npm install
npm run dev                         # development watcher; default port 3000
npm run typecheck                   # TypeScript validation
npm test                            # tests/framework.test.ts
npm run build                       # production compilation to .meu/
npx ryvax routes --json             # inspect manifest routes
npx ryvax doctor                    # inspect prerequisites
npx ryvax analyze --json --out-dir .meu
npx ryvax export --out-dir dist     # static site
npx ryvax deploy --out-dir dist     # Node deployment package
npx ryvax start --out-dir .meu --port 3000
npx ryvax migrate create add_users  # creates migrations/ paired files
```

The CLI reads `PORT` when `--port` is not supplied. The server listens on `0.0.0.0` by default through `createAppServer.listen`; `framework.config.*` can set `host`. In containers, expose port 3000 and set `PORT` as required by the platform.

## Security and reliability rules

Validate input before persistence. Separate authentication from authorization. Never serialize secrets into browser props. Bound body size, request timeouts, action bytes, retries, concurrency, and streams. Propagate cancellation. Keep provider-specific behavior inside adapters. Test 404, malformed input, 401, 403, unsupported methods, timeout, dependency failure, and shutdown. Build once and deploy the artifact that was verified.

## Anti-hallucination rules

- Do not install or introduce Next.js, Vite, Express, NestJS, React Router, or another framework by association.
- Do not create `next.config.*`, an unrequested `app/` or `pages/` tree, or a second router.
- Do not invent exports, hooks, CLI flags, config keys, environment variables, providers, or deployment guarantees.
- Do not edit `.meu/`, `dist/`, manifests, route bundles, or generated declarations manually.
- Do not call internal `src/*` modules through package imports unless `package.json` exports them.
- Do not assume a database, auth provider, queue provider, AI model provider, or cloud platform exists.
- Do not declare a task complete while available typecheck, tests, build, or runtime checks fail.

- Router: `src/router.ts`

- Runtime: `src/server.ts`
- Public contracts: `src/types.ts`
- Tests: `tests/framework.test.ts`
- Docs: `path/to/docs/` and `docs/site/`
- Repository: `https://github.com/kvantjs/ryvax.js`
